questions.question: Describe the water cycle in four steps.
questions.expected_answer: The Sun heats water in the sea, rivers and dams, and it evaporates into water vapour that rises. High in the cold sky, the water vapour condenses into tiny drops that form clouds. The drops join and fall as rain, or freeze and fall as hail or snow. The water runs into rivers and back to the sea, and the cycle starts again.

questions.question: Name the four changes of state that happen in the water cycle and where each one happens.
questions.expected_answer: Evaporating, when the Sun heats water in the sea, rivers or dams. Condensing, when water vapour cools high in the sky and forms clouds. Freezing, when water in very cold clouds turns into hail or snow. Melting, when snow and ice warm up and turn into liquid water.

questions.question: Why is rain fresh water even though much of it came from the salty sea?
questions.expected_answer: When sea water evaporates, only the water turns into vapour and rises. The salt stays behind in the sea, so the clouds and the rain that falls from them are fresh water.
